description: Advisory quality thresholds for Hairspring CI, retuned from recent `ci` workflow runs by scripts/auto-qa-tuner.mjs. Nothing in CI reads these values automatically: they are suggestions a human wires into ci.yml. The tuner only ever edits this file, and only through a bot-opened pull request that a human merges. It never pushes to main. The measured job is `PostgreSQL tests` (a single, stable job name; the Rust jobs are matrix jobs whose names change), so the timing suggestions describe that job and its test step, not the whole workflow.

bounds.rule: Each parameter has a baseline (authored by a human), hard min and max bounds, and maxStep (the largest change per run). `loosen` says which direction makes the gate weaker. The bound on the loosen side is the documented limit: the tuner can never move a value past it, however bad the data looks. The tuner only writes `value` and `history`; it never edits baseline, min, max or maxStep, so widening a bound is always a human edit in a reviewed PR. `--check` fails if a value is outside its bounds.
bounds.looseningIsBoundedBy: min or max on the loosen side, plus maxStep per run

parameters.description: Suggested timeout-minutes for the `PostgreSQL tests` job in ci.yml (today it is 60). Target is twice the observed p95 job duration (the six main runs sampled on 2026-11-20 took 6 to 12 minutes).
Suggested wall-clock budget for the `Test against PostgreSQL` step. Target is three times the observed p95 duration of that step (331 to 709 seconds in the six main runs sampled on 2026-11-20).

How many automatic re-runs of the PostgreSQL tests are tolerated before a failure counts. 0 unless at least 10 percent of recent successful runs needed a manual re-run (run_attempt above 1). The maximum is 1: more than one retry hides real failures.

Suggested minimum pass rate for the ci workflow on main over the window, below which the nightly report should be treated as unhealthy. Target is the observed pass rate minus 5 points. Cannot fall below 80.
